brief: Winter has no snow. The year has nine readers and a viewer who lands in February sees turned earth, bare trees and a skinned basin — the sky still rains. When a shower fires with `greyF()` high enough (warmth near midwinter), it falls as SNOW: slow drifting flakes instead of drops, and a `snowCover` scalar — rate-capped, per-cell variance via `hash(x, y+k)` like `fountainIce`, grain-matched to how each region is addressed — that whitens the cached ground (lawn, paving, plots), sits on roofs and awnings in the draw pass (never in `buildVolumes`), and melts over the days after as warmth climbs. It must be EXACTLY zero at SEASON_START (the anchor) by the algebra, so the summer town is byte-identical; it must not step (the cached layer buckets a quarter-hour — see the #39 law); and rain arriving on lying snow should thin it. Advertise it: one ticker line the first time it settles.
successLooksLike: A midwinter shot reads as winter from the wide view: white ground with dark paths worn through it, white roof edges, flakes instead of drops. `probes/`-style year fold shows cover 0 from spring to autumn, rising in the weeks around phase 0, max step per frame under a visible threshold; noon-at-anchor frame diff vs HEAD is 0.000; perf within noise.
avoid: Do not add a season or change SEASON_LEN. Do not make snow a boolean switch — it is a 0..1 like rainFall. Do not let footfall/desire-path wear interact with it this iteration; that is a follow-on cue.
